title: Filesystem, block size and the disk a database deserves

videos.script: A database is a program whose whole job is to put bytes on a disk and get them back. {{disk}} So the disk is not a detail somebody else chose. Its block size, its filesystem and its honesty about what it has written all reach your data. {{blocks}} PostgreSQL thinks in pages of eight kilobytes. The filesystem under it thinks in blocks of four. That mismatch is why a crash can tear a page in half, and lesson 8 showed the setting that repairs it. {{fsync}} This lesson measures a disk with the tool PostgreSQL ships for the job. It also shows what a disk that lies about flushing looks like in numbers. {{wal}} Then it gives the write-ahead log a filesystem of its own. {{full}} And then it fills two disks on purpose. A full tablespace costs you one statement. A full write-ahead log takes the whole server down, and it will not start again until you give it room. {{out}} You will see both errors exactly as PostgreSQL prints them, and the way out of each. A full disk is the most common emergency a database has. It is much calmer the second time. {{title}}
